subject: PO vs card procurement - FinOpsCo procurement readiness and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finopsco.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, procurement@finopsco.com
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: PO vs card procurement - Redwood next steps (post-call recap)

Hi Tom — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get you set up without surprises: 

Call recap:
- Use case: POC: internal AI assistant for sales ops (low latency, embeddings + chat).
- Expected initial spend: ~$3k–7k over 30–60 days for POC depending on usage.
- Procurement posture: AP prefers Purchase Order (PO) / invoice with Net30 for vendor onboarding, but engineering can pay by card for small POC if procurement approves.
- Security: you requested SOC 2 report, vendor questionnaire, and W-9/EIN.
- Commercial path options we discussed: direct invoice (PO), credit card for POC, or purchase via cloud marketplace (e.g., AWS Marketplace) — marketplace can simplify procurement later but adds vendor listing steps.

Proposed next steps:
1) I attached our vendor_onboarding_checklist.pdf and a short SOW draft for the POC (SOW-draft.docx). Please share any additional required documents or the right person at procurement to route items to.
2) Lauren (copied) will review contract terms and be available for legal redlines.
3) If procurement can issue a PO, we can proceed with direct invoice (Net30) and onboarding — we’ll need a billing contact and EIN for invoicing.
4) If you want to try a credit card for the initial POC (<$5k), confirm and I’ll share a quick payment link and enable the account same-day.
5) If marketplace is preferred, we can explore timelines (typically 4–6 weeks to enable and configure).

Would you please confirm which commercial path you prefer for the POC (PO / card / marketplace) and the billing contact? Once we have that we’ll send the SOW via DocuSign and kick off onboarding.

Attachments: vendor_onboarding_checklist.pdf (stub), SOW-draft.docx (stub)

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finopsco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finopsco.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 09:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PO vs card procurement - Redwood next steps (post-call recap)

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from procurement's side: 

- AP policy: Our default is PO + Net30. For small POCs under $5k we sometimes allow a corporate card to speed things up, subject to approval by the budget owner.
- Vendor onboarding: we require a completed vendor questionnaire, W-9, SOC 2 Type II (or equivalent), and proof of insurance. Our vendor team will also run a quick security review.
- Marketplace: if Redwood is available on AWS Marketplace with an SOW or SaaS entitlement, that could bypass some onboarding, but we need to confirm product parity and pricing. Marketplace purchases are preferred for ease of payment/chargeback.

Can you send the SOC 2 report and a sample invoice (showing company name/EIN and billing address) so our AP team can pre-check? Also include a suggested SOW value for the POC so I can route the budget approval.

If you can provide the docs this week we’ll start vendor onboarding and aim to issue a PO within ~10 business days. If procurement approves card for the POC, we’ll try to process it faster.

Thanks,
Tom Reynolds
Head of Procurement, FinOpsCo
Tom.Reynolds@finopsco.com | +1 (206) 555-0199
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finopsco.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, procurement@finopsco.com
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PO vs card procurement - Redwood next steps (docs and options)

Hi Tom — great, thanks. Attaching the items you requested and outlining the options so AP has everything in one place.

Attachments included (stubs):
- vendor_onboarding_checklist.pdf — our checklist that maps to your vendor requirements (W-9, SOC2, insurance, contact info).
- SOC2-report-2025.pdf — latest SOC 2 Type II report (redacted cover page + auditor stamp; full report available under NDA).
- sample_invoice.pdf — example invoice format showing company name, EIN, and billing address.
- SOW-draft.docx — short POC SOW (30 days / up to $5k) we can finalize.

Commercial options summary:
- Preferred (procurement friendly): Direct invoice via PO (Net30). Steps: vendor onboarding -> PO issued -> invoice -> enable account. Typical timeline: 7–14 business days after onboarding begins.
- Fastest (engineering-friendly): Corporate card for initial POC (<$5k). Steps: confirm budget owner/card approval -> payment link -> immediate enable.
- Marketplace: If you want AWS Marketplace, we can start that conversation, but it typically takes 4–6 weeks to list and sync pricing; good for long-term purchases and chargeback.

Suggested immediate next steps:
1) Procurement kickoff: If you confirm PO route, please assign a PoC and estimated PO amount (we recommend $6k to cover POC variability).
2) Legal: Lauren will start redlines on the SOW/contract once you confirm.
3) Tech enablement: once we have either PO or payment, we’ll schedule onboarding and provide temporary admin keys.

HubSpot link to deal + draft MSA: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890

Let me know if procurement would like us to send the SOW via DocuSign — we can do that today. Lauren — looping you in for contract support.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finopsco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finopsco.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PO vs card procurement - Redwood next steps (docs and options)

Marissa — received, thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. Next steps from procurement: 

- We will start vendor onboarding today. Security will request SOC2 directly to security@finopsco.com (please route the full report there under NDA).
- AP will aim to issue a PO within 10 business days; I will update you if we can move faster.
- For speed, I will ask the budget owner about using a corporate card for the <$5k POC and let you know by Friday.
- Please send the SOW via DocuSign to tom.reynolds@finopsco.com so legal can sign once procurement confirms terms.

If you can confirm billing name and EIN exactly as they should appear on the invoice, I’ll kick off the PO creation.

Thanks — Tom
Tom Reynolds
Head of Procurement, FinOpsCo
